L60: - **(a) Defining trait or umbrella phenotype.** The term is a defining trait of a named syndrome or disorder, introduced by a “characterized by”-type predicate (including consequence clauses inside that description), or it is listed as an umbrella phenotype with no individuated diagnosis. A trait is a feature of the named disorder, not a separate diagnosis of the patient, so this exclusion takes precedence over (ii). Such a term is not promoted. It keeps the label it would receive under Section 1 without this rule (Disease Class where it names a family of disorders; otherwise not annotated).

L52: - **(ii) Single organism or etiology.** The modifier pins the term to one named organism (species or genus) or to one named causal agent, such as a specific pathogen, toxin, drug, or chemical, or a named causative gene or gene variant. No predicate is needed. Inheritance patterns (“autosomal recessive,” “X-linked,” “inherited,” “familial”), onset or sex descriptors, and broad class descriptors (“viral,” “bacterial,” “fungal,” “genetic”) are **not** single etiologies. For those terms, (i) is required.
